title: ForecastProvenance
description:
Companion of a published set of v1 [`Forecast`] rows. Rows are only published beside a
companion for which [`ForecastProvenance::check_against`] holds, and only for the series whose
status is `forecast`: the series the publication policy admits.

artifact.description: Name of the series artifact that was forecast, e.g. `weekly-cases` (non-empty).

backtest.description:
The report-vintage backtest (the Texas DSHS 2025 outbreak total), when a committed report
exists for exactly this configuration.

horizon_weeks.description: Weeks forecast ahead of the origin week.

latest_data_week.description: Latest week with any row in the input series.

levels.description: Quantile levels of every row, strictly increasing in (0, 1).

origin_rule.description: How the origin week was chosen from the data (non-empty).

origin_week.description: Last week of data the forecast was allowed to use.

parameters.description:
One entry per configuration value, with the value the forecast ran with and its
citation (non-empty, unique).

publication_policy.description: The rule that decides which forecasts are published, with its thresholds.

run_count.description: Ensemble members behind every row's quantiles.

scope_note.description: What the skills do and do not say about the series above (non-empty).

seed.description:
Base seed of every series' ensemble (members derive from it, the geography and the
member index).

series.description: Every series considered, once each, in geography order.

series_backtest.description:
The backtest over the CDC NNDSS state series, when a committed report exists for exactly
this configuration.

statement.description: What the forecast is and is not, in plain words (non-empty).

BacktestSkill.description:
The measured skill of the method on its backtest, exactly as reported, with the scope it was
measured on. It is a statement about that series and period only.

by_horizon.description: The same scores per horizon, horizons 1, 2, ... in order.

coverage_50.description: Share of targets inside the central 50% interval (nominal 0.5).

coverage_90.description: Share of targets inside the central 90% interval (nominal 0.9).

forecast_dates.description: Forecast dates that produced a forecast.

limitations.description: What the backtest does not show (non-empty list of non-empty statements).

manifest_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the report-vintage manifest the backtest ran on.

mean_crps.description: Mean continuous ranked probability score over `targets`, in cases (lower is better).

mean_persistence_abs_error.description: Mean absolute error of carrying the origin week's count forward.

name.description:
Short name of what was backtested, for a sentence, e.g. `the 2025 West Texas outbreak`
(non-empty).

protocol.description: How the backtest respected the information cutoff, in words (non-empty).

report_path.description: Repository path of the committed report these numbers were read from.

report_sha256.description: SHA-256 of that report file exactly as read.

series.description: The series that was forecast and scored, in words (non-empty).

targets.description: Scored targets (forecast week by horizon), pooled.

CaseDefinition.description:
Which cases a weekly count includes. A count is only comparable with counts that share its
definition, so every row states it. Add a variant (in a new contract version) for any other
source definition; never reuse `Confirmed` for a count that includes other case statuses.

oneOf.description:
Only cases whose case status is confirmed under the source's case definition, with no
other status mixed in.

Confirmed cases plus cases whose case status is unknown, without the two being told
apart. This is what CDC's NNDSS measles publication criteria publish (event code 10140:
case status "confirmed" and "unknown"); the weekly query has no case-status field to
split them, so these counts must not be presented as confirmed cases.

ForecastInput.description: The series file the forecast was made from, hashed.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the input file exactly as read.

ForecastSeries.description: One series the pipeline considered: forecast, or not and why.

case_definition.description: What the series counts; a forecast describes cases under this definition only.

cases_in_window.description:
Cases in the estimation window ending at the origin week, when every count in it is
known.

skill.description: Which backtest, if any, measured this series' skill.

withheld.description:
Present exactly when `status` is `withheld`: why the forecast the method made is not
published.

ForecastStatus.description: Whether a series was forecast, and if the method made one, whether it is published.

oneOf.description: Forecast rows are published for the series: its measured skill meets the publication policy.

The method made a forecast but the publication policy does not admit it: no rows are
published, and `withheld` says why.

The method made no forecast (its minimum-count rule did not hold, or it refused the
projection): no number is published, and `reason` says why.

GeoId.description: Geography key: state FIPS (2 digits) or county FIPS (5 digits), zero-padded

InformationBasis.description:
How a backtest respected the information cutoff on *revisions* of the counts. A backtest on a
series whose revision history is not held is pseudo-real-time and must never be described as
real-time.

oneOf.description: Every forecast used only the report versions first seen by its forecast date.

One retrieval of the (revised) series is held: each forecast was given only the weeks up to
its origin, taken from that one retrieval. Revisions made after a forecast date are in the
counts the forecast saw.
oneOf.const: pseudo-real-time (revised counts truncated at each forecast date)

InsufficientReason.description:
Why the method made no forecast for a series (the renewal estimator's reason at the origin week,
or the method's refusal of a projection that grew past its limit).

oneOf.description: The estimation window would start before the series, or include its first week.
A count in the estimation window or the serial-interval look-back is missing.
Fewer cases in the window than the minimum-count threshold.
No cases in the look-back, so the window's cases have no infectors in the data.

A member's projected weekly mean passed the limit the method refuses to publish past (2^40).
Nothing is clipped: there is no forecast for the series.

MeasuredScores.description: The numbers of a measured evaluation, exactly as measured.

by_horizon.description: The same scores per horizon, horizons 1, 2, ... in order; the `n` sum to `targets`.

coverage_50.description: Share of targets inside the central 50% interval (nominal 0.5).

coverage_90.description: Share of targets inside the central 90% interval (nominal 0.9).

mean_crps.description: Mean continuous ranked probability score over `targets`, in cases (lower is better).

mean_persistence_abs_error.description: Mean absolute error of carrying the origin week's count forward.

targets.description: Scored targets (forecast week by horizon), pooled.

MmwrWeek.description: An MMWR year and week number (`week` is `1..=52` or `1..=53`).

week.description: Week of the MMWR year; 1 to 52, or 53 in a 53-week year.

year.description: MMWR year (not always the calendar year of every day in the week).

ParameterProvenance.description: One model parameter exactly as the scenario ran it, with its citation (#1400).

note.description: What the source supports and what it does not (non-empty).

url.description: Where to read it, when the source is a public page.

value.description: The value the scenario ran with, as it appears in the scenario's `parameters`.

PooledScores.description:
All series pooled: every scored target of every series, weighted equally, so the series with
the largest counts dominate a score in cases. A statement about the forecasts made where the
method's minimum-count rule held, never about any one series.

forecasts.description: (series, origin) forecasts with at least one scored target.

series.description: Series with at least one scored target.

PublicationPolicy.description:
The rule that decides whether a forecast is published, applied mechanically: a series' forecast
is published only if its method has a measured skill on that series that this policy admits. The
rule was written after the first state-series backtest result was known (that result is why it
exists) and before the code that applies it, and its thresholds are never tuned to a score. It
has an evidence floor (scored targets and distinct origin weeks) that applies to every kind of
evaluation alike, then a coverage floor and a ceiling on the error relative to the persistence
baseline. The thresholds travel with the companion so that the pipeline, this contract and the
web page check the same numbers.

maximum_crps_over_persistence.description:
The measured mean CRPS must be at most this multiple of the persistence baseline's mean
absolute error (1 is "no worse than carrying the latest count forward").

minimum_coverage_90.description: The measured 90% interval coverage must be at least this.

minimum_origin_weeks.description:
...from at least this many distinct origin weeks (the 8 horizons of one origin are not
independent evidence). Applies to the report-vintage backtest and to the series backtest
alike: a series with less evidence has no measured skill, whatever its scores.

minimum_targets.description: The evidence floor: at least this many scored targets of the series itself...

rule.description: The rule in plain words, with the reasons for its thresholds (non-empty).

SeriesBacktest.description:
A backtest of the forecast over a family of series (#1503), with the scope and information
basis it was measured on. It is a statement about those series and that period only.

basis.description: Whether the information cutoff covered revisions of the counts.

by_series.description: Every series the backtest ran on, once each, in geography order.

input_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the source snapshot the backtest ran on.

limitations.description: What this evaluation does not show (non-empty list of non-empty statements).

minimum_origin_weeks.description: ...from at least this many distinct origin weeks. Fixed before any score was computed.

minimum_targets.description: The floor for a measured skill: at least this many scored targets...

name.description:
Short name of what was backtested, for a sentence, e.g. `the CDC NNDSS state series`
(non-empty).

pooled.description: Every series pooled; absent when even the pooled result is below the floor.

protocol.description: How the information cutoff was respected, and what that may hide, in words (non-empty).

provisional_weeks.description:
Recent weeks treated as provisional: the origin is the latest week less these, and the same
newest weeks are never used as truth.

report_path.description: Repository path of the committed report these numbers were read from.

report_sha256.description: SHA-256 of that report file exactly as read.

seed.description: Base seed of the backtest (and of the published forecast).

series.description: What was forecast and scored, in words, including what was not scored (non-empty).

SeriesBacktestEntry.description:
What the evaluation scored for one series. The scores are present exactly when the series
reached the evaluation's floor: below it the series has insufficient data for a skill, however
its scores would have looked.

forecasts.description: Origins at which the method forecast this series (its minimum-count rule held).

measured.description: The measured skill; present exactly when `targets` and `origin_weeks` reach the floor.

origin_weeks.description: Distinct origin weeks with at least one scored target.

SeriesSkill.description:
Whether a series has a measured skill, and which evaluation says so. A forecast method is only
as good as its tests on the data it is run on: a series no backtest scored has no measured
skill, and says so.

oneOf.description:
The series is the one the report-vintage backtest scored (same geography, case definition
and source); its measured skill is in `backtest`.

The series was scored in `series_backtest` with enough targets from enough origin weeks to
state a skill; its numbers are that entry's `measured`.

The series was part of `series_backtest`, but too few targets or origin weeks were scored
for it to state a skill. Nothing is measured about it, and no other series' number is
evidence about it.
oneOf.const: insufficient data for a measured skill

oneOf.description: No backtest scored this series. Nothing has been measured about how this forecast will do.

coverage_50.description: Share of targets inside the central 50% interval; absent when `n` is 0.

coverage_90.description: Share of targets inside the central 90% interval; absent when `n` is 0.

mean_crps.description: Mean CRPS in cases; absent when `n` is 0.

WithheldReason.description: Why a forecast the method made is not published.

oneOf.description: No backtest scored this series, so nothing is measured about how its forecast does.
A backtest ran on this series but scored too little for a measured skill.
The series has a measured skill, and it does not meet the publication policy.
